use_cases.name: Run payrolls of different frequencies side by side
use_cases.goal: Run monthly, semi-monthly, weekly and daily-wage payrolls for different pay groups in parallel, each with its own calendar, cut-offs and locks.

stakeholders.interest: Daily-wage and contract workers are paid on their own cycle without waiting for the monthly run.
Every run posts its own journal into the correct accounting period.
Monthly statutory contributions aggregate correctly across weekly runs.

use_cases.trigger: A pay calendar reaches the cut-off date for a pay group, for example the weekly cycle for daily-wage workers at Peenya Works.
preconditions: Each pay group has a calendar defining frequency, period dates, cut-off, lock and pay dates.
Daily-wage workers (WC-CONT) are assigned to a weekly pay group with wage type daily (RL-290).
postconditions_success: The run for the pay group is computed, approved and disbursed on its own calendar; locks on one group do not block another.
postconditions_failure: The run stays open with blocking flags listed; other pay groups' runs are unaffected.

main_flow.action: Opens the weekly run for pay group PLANT-BLR-DW for 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 per its calendar.
Resolves the population from assignments active in the week, including E1032 and E1033.
Confirms attendance for the week is final for the pay group.
Locks inputs for the weekly run only; the monthly PLANT-BLR run stays open.
Computes daily-wage earnings from paid days and the daily rate, and deductions for the week.
Accumulates statutory wage bases across the month's weekly runs so contributions are reconciled monthly.
Reviews variance and approves the run.
Prepares the bank file and the run's own journal for the week.
Credits wages on the weekly pay date.

alternate_flows.condition: A semi-monthly group reaches its 15th-of-month cut-off.
steps: The platform opens a semi-monthly run for the first half and processes it the same way.

alternate_flows.condition: A worker moved from the weekly to the monthly group mid-period.
steps: Each run includes only the days covered by the assignment in its group.

exception_flows.condition: A critical audit flag is open on the weekly run.
exception_flows.handling: Approval is blocked until the flag is resolved or waived by an authorised role.

exception_flows.condition: A weekly run's cumulative earnings cross the ESI threshold within the contribution period.
exception_flows.handling: Contribution continues to the end of the period and the case is flagged.

nfrs: A weekly run of 2,000 daily-wage workers computes in under 2 minutes.
Locks are scoped per run; locking one pay group never blocks input to another.

user_stories.want: a weekly run for daily-wage workers alongside the monthly run
user_stories.so_that: contract workers are paid every week

acceptance.given: PLANT-BLR-DW has a weekly calendar and PLANT-BLR is monthly
acceptance.when: the weekly run for 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 is locked
acceptance.then: attendance input for the monthly run remains editable

acceptance.given: E1032 worked 6 days at a daily rate of 72,000 paise
acceptance.then: gross earnings are 432,000 paise

user_stories.want: monthly statutory contributions reconciled across weekly runs

acceptance.given: four weekly runs in November 2026
acceptance.then: the PF wage base for each worker equals the sum of the four weekly bases

acceptance.given: a worker whose weekly earnings cross the ESI threshold in week 3
acceptance.then: ESI continues and the case is flagged

user_stories.want: a separate journal for every run
user_stories.so_that: weekly wage cost lands in the right accounting period

acceptance.given: a weekly run paid on 2026-11-10
acceptance.then: a journal for that run is emitted with posting date 2026-11-10

acceptance.given: two weekly runs in the same month
acceptance.then: I see two journals with different run identifiers

use_cases.name: Model take-home pay before submitting a choice
use_cases.goal: Let an employee model the take-home effect of choices such as tax regime, voluntary provident fund, flexible-benefit allocation or a loan before submitting them.

stakeholders.interest: Understands the real monthly and annual effect of a choice before committing.
Fewer mid-year reversals and queries after declarations are submitted.

use_cases.trigger: An employee opens the net-pay what-if from the tax declaration, benefits or loan screen.
preconditions: The employee has a salary structure and year-to-date payroll results.
Current rule pack versions for income tax and statutory deductions are published.
postconditions_success: The employee sees projected monthly and annual take-home for each scenario and may submit the chosen option through the normal request flow.
postconditions_failure: No scenario is saved as a submission and live payroll inputs are unchanged.

main_flow.action: Opens the what-if tool and sees the current projection: regime, VPF, flexible-benefit split and any loan recovery.
Creates a scenario switching to the other tax regime and adding 5% VPF.
Runs the gross-to-net graph in simulation mode using the current rule pack versions and year-to-date results.
Projects tax to year end under the scenario and shows monthly and annual take-home against the current choice.
Adds a second scenario with a company loan EMI and compares all three.
Explains each difference line by line, naming the component and rule that changed it.
Chooses a scenario and submits it through the declaration or loan application flow.

alternate_flows.condition: The employee decides not to change anything.
steps: The scenarios are kept privately for 30 days and then deleted.

exception_flows.handling: The scenario shows the eligibility limit and the maximum EMI allowed.

exception_flows.condition: A regime switch is not permitted at this point in the year.
exception_flows.handling: The scenario is shown for information and the submit option is disabled with the reason.

nfrs: A scenario result is returned in under 2 s.
Simulation never writes to payroll inputs or results.

user_stories.want: to compare take-home under both tax regimes
user_stories.so_that: I choose the regime that leaves me better off

acceptance.given: I am E1010 Nandita Bose with year-to-date results to October 2026
acceptance.then: I see projected annual tax and monthly take-home for both regimes

acceptance.given: the projected difference is ₹1,850 a month
acceptance.then: each line shows the component and rule that changed

user_stories.want: to see the effect of VPF and a loan EMI together
user_stories.so_that: I know what I will actually receive each month

acceptance.given: a scenario with 5% VPF and a loan EMI of ₹6,000
acceptance.then: monthly take-home shows both deductions applied

acceptance.given: an EMI above my eligibility
acceptance.then: the maximum allowed EMI is shown

user_stories.want: simulations kept separate from live inputs
user_stories.so_that: a what-if never alters a payroll run

acceptance.given: 500 employees ran scenarios during the November window
acceptance.then: no input row originates from a scenario that was not submitted

acceptance.given: a submitted declaration
acceptance.then: it references the scenario the employee chose

use_cases.name: Trace a payslip line to its inputs, rules and approvals
use_cases.goal: Allow payroll and auditors to trace any payslip line back to its inputs, rules, rule versions and the run's approval history.

stakeholders.interest: Can verify any figure without asking the payroll team to reconstruct it.
Answers employee and audit queries quickly from evidence.

use_cases.trigger: An auditor or payroll manager selects a payslip line to investigate.
preconditions: Every payslip line stores the node, inputs, output and rule pack version that produced it (RL-273).
The run snapshot hashes inputs, rule pack versions and configuration (RL-251).
postconditions_success: The investigator sees the full lineage of the line and can recompute it to the paisa; the trace is logged.
postconditions_failure: If recomputation does not match, a critical discrepancy is raised for the payroll manager.

main_flow.action: Opens the September 2026 PLANT-PUN payslip of E1044 Rahul Gaikwad and selects the loan recovery line.
Shows the DAG node, its inputs, output in paise and the rule pack version that produced it.
Drills from each input to its source record, such as the loan schedule and the attendance days.
Shows the source record versions as at the run's snapshot timestamp.
Opens the run's approval history: who locked, reviewed, approved and prepared disbursement, with times.
Requests recomputation of the line from the snapshot.
Recomputes and confirms the result matches to the paisa, recording the trace in the audit ledger.

alternate_flows.condition: The investigator starts from a payroll register total rather than a payslip.
steps: The platform lists contributing payslip lines, from which one is selected.

exception_flows.condition: Recomputation differs from the stored result.
exception_flows.handling: A critical discrepancy is raised to the payroll manager and the line is marked under investigation.

exception_flows.condition: The auditor's scope excludes the payroll group.
exception_flows.handling: Amounts return null and the trace shows only structure.

nfrs: A line trace opens in under 2 s.
Recomputation of one employee's payslip from the snapshot completes in under 5 s.

user_stories.want: to drill from a payslip line to its inputs and rule version
user_stories.so_that: I can verify the figure independently

acceptance.given: E1044's September loan recovery line of ₹8,400
acceptance.then: I see the loan schedule row, recovery node and rule pack version

acceptance.given: I request recomputation
acceptance.then: the recomputed value equals ₹8,400 to the paisa

user_stories.want: the run's approval history on every trace
user_stories.so_that: I can show who authorised the figures

acceptance.given: the September PLANT-PUN run
acceptance.when: I open approval history from any of its payslips
acceptance.then: lock, review, approval and disbursement steps show actor and timestamp

acceptance.given: a recomputation mismatch
acceptance.then: I receive a critical discrepancy alert naming the line

user_stories.want: to start from a register total and reach the lines behind it
user_stories.so_that: I can explain a variance quickly

acceptance.given: PF employer contribution for PLANT-PUN rose 6% in September
acceptance.then: contributing payslip lines are listed, largest first

acceptance.given: I select one line
acceptance.then: its inputs are shown as at the snapshot timestamp

use_cases.name: Hold and release an individual's net pay
use_cases.goal: Allow payroll to hold an individual's net pay with a reason and release it in the same or a later run with full audit.

stakeholders.interest: Is told a hold has been placed and paid promptly once it is released.
Held amounts sit in a liability account and are not lost.
Every hold and release has a reason and an authorised approver.

use_cases.trigger: HR or payroll identifies a reason to withhold pay, for example unauthorised absence, pending bank verification or unreturned assets.
preconditions: The employee's payroll result for the run is computed.
Hold reasons and the approver for holds are configured.
postconditions_success: Net pay is excluded from the bank file and recorded as held; on release, it is paid in the chosen run with its original period and reason recorded.
postconditions_failure: No hold is applied and net pay flows to disbursement as normal.

main_flow.action: Requests a salary hold for E1022 Mohan Joseph citing unverified bank details after a change inside the payroll window.
Places the hold on the October run with reason code and expected review date.
Routes the hold through its approval chain.
Approves the hold.
Keeps the payslip computed but excludes net pay from the bank file and posts it to a held-salary liability.
Tells the employee a hold has been placed, with the reason category and HR contact.
Releases the hold once the bank details are verified, choosing the November run or an off-cycle run.
Adds the held amount to the chosen run as a release line referencing the original period and clears the liability.

alternate_flows.condition: The issue is resolved before October disbursement is prepared.
steps: The hold is released in the same run and the net pay returns to the October bank file.
The held amount is carried into full-and-final settlement.

exception_flows.condition: Disbursement for the run is already prepared.
exception_flows.handling: The hold cannot be applied to this run; payroll is told to recall the payment or hold the next run.
The hold is removed and net pay remains in the bank file.

nfrs: A hold applied before disbursement preparation is reflected in the bank file within 1 minute.
Every hold and release is retrievable by employee, run and reason for 8 years.

user_stories.want: to hold one employee's net pay with a reason
user_stories.so_that: pay is not released while an issue is open

acceptance.given: E1022's October net pay is ₹27,640 and a hold is approved
acceptance.when: the October bank file is prepared
acceptance.then: E1022 is excluded and ₹27,640 is posted to held-salary liability

acceptance.given: the October bank file is already prepared
acceptance.then: the hold is refused and the message says to recall or use the next run

user_stories.want: to release a held amount in a later run
user_stories.so_that: the employee is paid as soon as the issue is closed

acceptance.given: a ₹27,640 hold from October
acceptance.when: I release it into the November run
acceptance.then: November shows a release line referencing October and the liability is cleared

acceptance.given: the release is urgent
acceptance.then: the amount is paid in that run with the same reference

user_stories.want: to be told when my pay is held and why
user_stories.so_that: I can resolve the issue quickly

acceptance.given: a hold is approved on my October pay
acceptance.then: I receive a notification with the reason category and HR contact

acceptance.given: the hold is released
acceptance.then: I am notified of the pay date
